newsitem.title: UK: Ramco shares up on Caspian pipeline news.
newsitem.headline: Ramco shares up on Caspian pipeline news.

text.p: Shares in Ramco Energy Plc rose 37-1/2p to a record peak of 10.90 stg on Friday following news that an agreement had been signed to build an oil pipeline linking Caspian Sea oilfields to Russia, market makers said.
"Ramco doesn't directly benefit from this deal but it is still good news. It's more of a confidence boost for companies that are doing business in the area," one market maker said.

The Caspian Pipeline Consortium(CPC), which plans to build the 1,500 km (940 mile) pipeline from Kazakhstan's Tengiz oilfield to Russia's Black Sea oil export outlet at Novorossiisk, signed a "final agreement" with the Russian government in Moscow on Friday.
Ramco, the Aberdeen-based oil exploration company, has interests in Azerbaijan's section of the Caspian but will not use the pipeline to transport Azeri crude to the Russian port.
However, Ramco is considering projects in Kazakhastan, which could eventually benefit from the CPC pipeline.

"We are looking in Kazakhstan but they are in relatively early stages," Ramco finance director Steven Bertram told Reuters. "Obviously if we are successful there it is possible that the CPC pipeline will be of benefit."
